prompt:
Initial request:
I’m choosing an e-reader mainly for novels and U.S. public-library ebooks. Compare exactly these three new base models: Kobo Libra Colour, Kobo Clara Colour, and Kindle Paperwhite (12th generation, 2024 release). My pre-tax device budget is $180. Give me a compact comparison table and a complete ranking of all three. Low weight matters more to me than screen size. Use only the facts in source_pack.md and cite them with its bracketed source IDs.

Clarification:
Every option must be assessed against these must-haves: an adjustable warm front light, IPX8 waterproofing, at least 16 GB of storage, and a documented U.S. public-library borrowing route. Physical page-turn buttons are a nice-to-have, not a requirement. Discuss ergonomics, but do not invent handedness preferences, case weights, or other facts the source pack does not give. Keep sourced facts separate from your recommendations.

Correction:
I gave you two details backward: the pre-tax device budget is $270, not $180, and screen size matters more than low weight. Only those two points change. Page-turn buttons remain merely a nice-to-have, and every other instruction still stands.

Final delivery:
Write the finished comparison to comparison.md now; do not give me a plan or a description of what you would write. Make it 450–650 words and use the headings “Verified comparison,” “Recommendation,” and “Uncertainties,” in that order. Put the factual table and source-grounded comparison under “Verified comparison.” Under “Recommendation,” give a numbered 1-to-3 ranking, name one clear winner, and explain the tradeoffs using my corrected priorities. Under “Uncertainties,” explicitly identify what the sources do not settle or what may vary. Cite each sentence or table row that makes a product fact claim; do not cite my preferences as though they were external facts. Preserve every earlier instruction except where my correction directly conflicts with it.
